note: PRIOR-PREDICTIVE (forward push of Andrew's 2-4 lb box-mass prior through M(theta) -> fundamental frequency f1). NOT a posterior; no sampler. The next card UPDATES this with the tap test.

forward_map.method: direct monotone linear interpolation of f1(m) (NOT a parametric law: the box mode crosses the fundamental near 2-2.5 lb, box KE-in-mode-1 jumps 0.232->0.245, so a single 1/f^2 law does not fit; interpolation is exact at the grid)

identifiability_caveat: The box does NOT cleanly own a single mode across 2-4 lb: its mode CROSSES the fundamental near 2-2.5 lb (box KE-in-mode-1 jumps 0.232->0.245) and its energy otherwise smears across a veering 17-45 Hz shield cluster (no single clean peak). f1 stays monotone in box mass (interlacing) but shifts only ~0.8 Hz across the whole prior and is partly confounded with valve mass. => the tap test resolves box mass only WEAKLY from f1; the next card should use the 17-45 Hz cluster (and ideally a sensor ON the box) to update it, and expect box-mass vs valve-mass confounding.
plain_english: Andrew's 2-4 lb prior maps the FUNDAMENTAL to 13.6 Hz, 95% band [13.0, 14.1] Hz -- but that mode is valve-dominated, so the box mass barely moves it. Honest read: a single-peak tap test under-resolves this box mass; see identifiability_caveat.
